source.title: Mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes: consequences and open questions

accepted.question_text: For the periodic Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process with L sites, fixed particle density ρ, activity K equal to the total number of jumps, and activity counting field s, determine the scaled cumulant generating function ψ_K^SSEP(s) in the hyperuniform large-activity regime s > 0 with s of order one, beyond the diffusive Edwards-Wilkinson scaling s = λ/L². Equivalently, can the ASEP-current cumulant series obtained from the mapping ψ_K^SSEP(s) = (2/(p+q)) ψ_Q^ASEP(µ), with e^{-2µ} = p/q and e^{-s} = cosh(µ), be resummed or transformed despite divergences when q/p approaches roots of unity, and can one obtain a positive-s parametric representation analogous to the known negative-s representation?
accepted.context_brief: Hyperuniform SSEP activity SCGF beyond diffusive scaling

evidence.quote:
Understanding how the SCGF behaves for s > 0 (beyond the
diﬀusive regime) is not trivial and still an open question, as we detail in the next subsection.

We were not able to perform a resummation or
a transformation of this series that would allow one to cure this behavior.

The question of computing the series (3.33) for s > 0 thus remains open, and would yield an interesting
description of the hyperuniform phase beyond the diﬀusive regime described in Sec. 3.2. The aim would
be to ﬁnd the equivalent of the parametric representation of Eqs. (3.18)-(3.21) for ψSSEP
K (s), but valid for
s > 0.

The
question remains open to understand how the series (3.33) can be resummed in order to understand how
the SCGF ψSSEP
K (s) behaves in the hyperuniform regime s > 0 for s = O(L0) (i.e. beyond the diﬀusive
regime). Since the singularities occur when q
p are unit roots, it would be interesting to see if the results
of Refs. [117–120] could be used in some way.

accepted.question_text: What is the precise relationship, if any, between the KPZ scaling governing activity fluctuations in the time-reversal-symmetric SSEP and the KPZ scalings recently found for SO(3) classical spin dynamics and for the quantum Heisenberg magnet?
accepted.context_brief: Comparison with KPZ scaling in spin dynamics

evidence.quote:
The occurrence of such KPZ scaling could be interestingly compared
to those recently uncovered by Prosen and coworkers for SO(3) classical spin dynamics [115] or for the
quantum Heisenberg magnet [116].

accepted.question_text: Can Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz methods and their extensions compute corrections to the Edwards-Wilkinson activity-fluctuation scaling at large λ, where s = λ/L² in the diffusive regime, and can those corrections be matched to the next orders of the small-s expansion in the finite-s KPZ regime?
accepted.context_brief: TBA corrections connecting EW and KPZ expansions

evidence.quote:
Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz and its extensions allows one to obtain corrections to the EW scal-
ing (3.5) at large λ, as done in Ref. [58]: it could be instructive to see how the expansion matches the next
orders of the small- s expansion (3.22)-(3.23) in the KPZ regime.

accepted.question_text: For the coordinate Bethe Ansatz description of SSEP activity fluctuations, how does the solution cross over from the Edwards-Wilkinson scaling regime, with s = λ/L² at fixed λ and large L, to the KPZ scaling regime, with finite s and large L?
accepted.context_brief: Coordinate Bethe Ansatz crossover from EW to KPZ scaling

evidence.quote:
Related to this, the existence of two
diﬀerent scalings with L (EW and KPZ) on each side of the transition could be interesting to describe
how the coordinate Bethe Ansatz behaves as one crosses over from the EW scaling regime ( s = λ/L2
with ﬁxed λ and large L), studied in Ref. [47], to the KPZ scaling regime (ﬁnite s and large L).

accepted.question_text: Can the similarity-transform mapping between the joint scaled cumulant generating functions of current and activity in ASEP models be related to previously known mappings for current large-deviation functions or for steady-state large deviations?
accepted.context_brief: Relation to other exclusion-process large-deviation mappings

evidence.quote:
Also, the mapping we have used could be related to other ones that have been found for the current
LDFs [19,20] or for the steady-state large deviations [121,122].

accepted.question_text: For the deformed Markov matrices that bias exclusion-process trajectories by current or activity, can the spectral gap be computed by Bethe Ansatz near dynamical phase transitions and for nonzero Legendre parameters? In particular, under the mapping between the SSEP activity-biased operator M and the ASEP current-biased operator W, does the gap of M scale as L^{-3/2} for sufficiently large |s|, which would imply dynamical exponent 3/2 for SSEP activity large deviations beyond the diffusive regime?
accepted.context_brief: Gap scaling of deformed activity/current evolution operators

evidence.quote:
Last, studies of the gap in the deformed
evolution operator (which is in principle possible within the Bethe Ansatz approach) could shed light
on the ﬁnite-time scalings close to a DPT, in the spirit of previous works in diﬀusive [123] and super-
diﬀusive [124] models, or in so-called large- N models [55,125].

It would be
interesting to extend their computation to the case of the deformed Markov matrices we have considered.
For instance, if through the mapping between M and W , the gap of M scales as 1/L3/2 for large enough
|s|, it would imply that the dynamical exponent of the large deviations of activity in the SSEP is 3 /2 for
deviations beyond the diﬀusive regime (where the dynamical exponent is 2).

accepted.question_text: For an open WASEP with left and right reservoir densities both equal to 1/2, bulk asymmetry p/q = exp(2ν₁/L), and activity bias s = λ/L², determine whether particle-hole symmetry is broken when λ exceeds ν₁²/2, the range not accessible through the real-parameter mapping to a current-conditioned WASEP. Here symmetry breaking means that the optimal density profile for the activity-conditioned large deviation is no longer flat.

accepted.question_text: For the open SSEP with equal boundary reservoir densities ρ_a = ρ_b = 1/2, conditioned by activity in the diffusive scaling s = λ/L², is there critical behavior near λ = −π²/2, possibly including the onset of power-law correlations, even though the mapped WASEP criterion predicts no particle-hole symmetry breaking for ν₁ = 0?

Mapped the PDF structure: main open-question regions are section 3.5 on non-diffusive s > 0 activity fluctuations, section 3.7 on the XXZ fixed-magnetization conjecture, section 4.3 on open WASEP/SSEP activity-conditioned symmetry breaking, and section 5 conclusion/outlook.
Section 3.5 and the conclusion explicitly state that computing or resumming the positive-s series for the SSEP activity SCGF remains open.
Section 3.7 formulates a conjecture for the XXZ spin-chain correlation coefficient at arbitrary fixed magnetization.
The conclusion identifies comparison with KPZ scalings in SO(3) classical spin dynamics and the quantum Heisenberg magnet as an open direction.
The conclusion identifies matching TBA corrections to the KPZ small-s expansion as an open direction.
The conclusion identifies the coordinate Bethe Ansatz crossover from EW to KPZ scaling as an open direction.
The conclusion identifies relations between the activity/current mapping and other large-deviation mappings as an open direction.
The conclusion identifies gap computations for the deformed evolution operators and their dynamical-exponent implications as an open direction.
Section 4.3 states that the mapping cannot decide particle-hole symmetry breaking for λ beyond the real-parameter accessible range.
Section 4.3 states a possible SSEP critical behavior around λ = -π²/2 despite no symmetry breaking.
